blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is a Service, from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: A StatefulSet, later in the file, needs a headless Service to give each Pod its own DNS name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create first: a Service

blocks.title: A headless Service
blocks.what: This Service is called db. clusterIP: None makes it headless: no shared address.
blocks.why: Lookups then return each Pod, and each StatefulSet Pod gets a name such as db-0.db.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Service gets a shared address, and Pods get no names of their own.
blocks.comment: No shared address, so each Pod gets its own DNS name
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None

blocks.title: Which Pods?
blocks.what: The selector finds Pods labelled app: db.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Service finds no Pods, so no names are created.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db

blocks.title: Add the StatefulSet
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a StatefulSet called db, from apps/v1.
blocks.why: A StatefulSet is like a Deployment, but each Pod keeps its name and its own disk.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db

blocks.title: Names and copies
blocks.what: serviceName links the headless Service. Two copies, managed by the label app: db.
blocks.why: The Pods are called db-0 and db-1, and start in that order.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StatefulSet, because it needs a selector.
blocks.comment: Two Pods, db-0 and db-1, named through the db Service
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template gives each Pod the label app: db.
blocks.why: The labels must match the selector, as in a Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StatefulSet, because it would have nothing to create.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: db

blocks.title: What each Pod runs
blocks.what: busybox writes its own name and the time to /data/log, then sleeps.
blocks.why: It stands in for a database. Each line shows which Pod wrote it.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StatefulSet, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: Note the Pod’s name and start time in /data/log
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: db
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) started at $(date) >> /data/log && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Where the disk appears
blocks.what: The volume named data appears at /data.
blocks.why: Each Pod writes to its own disk here.
blocks.ifRemoved: Files under /data are lost whenever a Pod is replaced.
blocks.comment: The Pod’s own disk appears at /data
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: db
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) started at $(date) >> /data/log && sleep 3600"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data

blocks.title: A disk for each Pod
blocks.what: volumeClaimTemplates makes one claim per Pod from this template, named data-db-0 and data-db-1.
blocks.why: A replaced Pod gets back the claim with its name, and so its data.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StatefulSet, because the mount names a volume that does not exist.
blocks.comment: Make a claim called data for each Pod
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: db
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) started at $(date) >> /data/log && sleep 3600"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:

blocks.title: What kind of disk?
blocks.what: Each claim uses the auto-ebs StorageClass from the storage lesson: 1Gi, one node at a time. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Each Pod gets its own EBS volume.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the claim template, because it must say how much storage it needs.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: db
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) started at $(date) >> /data/log && sleep 3600"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        storageClassName: auto-ebs
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteOnce
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 1Gi

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version. Services are in core v1; StatefulSets are in apps/v1.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.Service:kind: A Service gives Pods a name to be found by.
notes.StatefulSet:kind: Runs Pods that each keep their name and their own disk.
notes.Service:metadata.name: The Service name, db. Pod names end in .db.
notes.StatefulSet:metadata.name: The StatefulSet name. Pods are called db-0, db-1, and so on.
notes.Service:spec: The desired state of the Service.
notes.StatefulSet:spec: The desired state of the StatefulSet.
notes.spec.clusterIP: None makes the Service headless: lookups return each Pod’s own address.
notes.Service:spec.selector: Pods with all of these labels get DNS names.
notes.spec.serviceName: The headless Service that gives each Pod its DNS name.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to run: two.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this StatefulSet manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: db.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Add the Pod’s name and the time to /data/log, then sleep.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].volumeMo: Where volumes appear inside the container.
Which volume: data, from the claim template.
notes.spec.volumeClaimTemplates: Templates for claims. Each Pod gets its own claim from each template.
notes.spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata.nam: data. The claims are called data-db-0 and data-db-1.
notes.spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.storage: auto-ebs, the StorageClass from the storage lesson.
notes.spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.accessM: How each volume can be used.
ReadWriteOnce: one node at a time.
notes.spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.resourc: How much storage each claim needs.

tryIt.result: Creates the auto-ebs StorageClass from the storage lesson, with its Pod and claim.
Creates the headless Service and the StatefulSet.
db-0 and db-1 are Running. db-1 started only after db-0 was ready.
data-db-0 and data-db-1 are Bound: one EBS volume each.
Removes db-0. The StatefulSet creates it again with the same name.
Prints two lines from db-0. The new Pod got the same disk back.
Prints db-0’s own address. busybox’s nslookup needs the full name.
Removes the Service and the StatefulSet.
Both claims are still there. A StatefulSet keeps its disks, so data is not lost by accident.
Removes both claims, and Auto Mode deletes their EBS volumes.

questions.question: What are the two Pods called?
answers: db-0 and db-1, kept when they are replaced
questions.explain: A StatefulSet numbers its Pods from 0, and a replacement keeps the same name.

questions.question: db-0 is replaced. Which disk does the new db-0 get?
questions.explain: Claims are named after the template and the Pod, so db-0 always gets data-db-0.

questions.question: Why does the Service have clusterIP: None?
answers: So each Pod gets its own DNS name
questions.explain: A headless Service has no shared address. Each StatefulSet Pod gets a name such as db-0.db.

fix.message: The StatefulSet "db" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[0].name: Not found: "disk"
fix.explain: The mount asks for a volume called disk, but the claim template is called data.
fix.fix: Use the claim template’s name: data.
